On a phone with your app installed, tap **Open in app**. Then open the site again and tap the close button.

**You should see:** your app opens on the link's screen, and the tap appears in Dashboard → Analytics. After you close the bar, it stays hidden on that browser for 30 days.

sections.page: Smart app banner for mobile web
sections.markdown:
| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `link` | (required) | Your Strait link. Opened as is. |
| `title`, `subtitle` | (title required) | Text on the bar, shown as plain text. |
| `icon` | none | Icon URL, shown at 40×40. |
| `button` | `Open in app` | Button text. |
| `theme` | `auto` | `light`, `dark`, or `auto` to follow the visitor's setting. |
| `position` | `top` | `top` pushes the page down; `bottom` floats over it. |
| `accent`, `accentText` | dark button | Button colour and its text colour, any CSS colour. |
| `dismissDays` | `30` | Days it stays hidden after the visitor closes it. |
| `inApp`, `appUserAgent` | none | Hide it inside your own app (step 4). |
| `force` | `false` | Show it everywhere, even after a close. For previews only. |

`banner()` returns `{ element, dismiss, remove }`, or `null` when it isn't shown.

sections.page: Smart app banner for mobile web
sections.markdown:
Nothing. The banner makes no requests and sets no cookies. It stores one value in the visitor's browser, `strait.banner.dismissed`, the time they closed it. The only thing recorded is the tap on your link, by Strait, the same as for any link. If the browser blocks storage, the banner still works and simply shows again on the next visit.

:::note Safari's own banner
Safari has a built-in banner (the `apple-itunes-app` meta tag). Use one or the other on iPhone, or visitors see two bars. Safari's banner appears only in Safari and doesn't go through your Strait link.
:::

sections.page: Smart app banner for mobile web
sections.markdown:
- **Nothing shows on your computer.** That's by design. Use a phone, or add `force: true` while you check the styling.
- **Nothing shows on a phone either.** You closed it in the last 30 days on that browser. Clear the site's data, or use `force: true` once. A link that isn't `https://` or `http://` also stops it.
- **The app opens on its home screen.** The link's destination is your home page, or the app doesn't route links yet. Check the destination in Dashboard → Links and set up [receiving links](https://straitlink.in/docs/sdks/react-native/receive-links/) in the app.

sections.page: Smart app banner for mobile web
sections.markdown:
- [Web SDK](https://straitlink.in/docs/sdks/web/): resolve a deferred link on a first visit to your web app.
- [Analytics: how we count](https://straitlink.in/docs/analytics/): where banner taps show up.

sections.page: Store sheet (beta) — install another app without leaving yours
sections.markdown: **Beta.** The store sheet is new and not in a released SDK version yet. On iPhone, the deep link after install relies on install matching, which is in beta. Taps from the store sheet are recorded but not billed during the beta.

sections.page: Store sheet (beta) — install another app without leaving yours
sections.section: What it is, and where it works
sections.markdown:
Some apps show the store as a sheet *inside* the app: the user taps **Install**, installs, and never leaves. The app showing the sheet does this with a store API. A link can't make another company's app do it, so a link tapped inside a social app's in-app browser can't open a store sheet there.

The store sheet works where **your app is the host**:

- recommending a sibling app (a "lite", seller, partner or driver app) from your main app,
- "invite a friend to app B" flows inside app A,
- web content your app shows in its own WebView, when that page calls your app.

What Strait adds is the deep link. A bare store sheet drops context: the user installs app B, and app B doesn't know which screen they wanted. With `openStoreSheet`, app B opens on the linked screen after install.

sections.page: Store sheet (beta) — install another app without leaving yours
sections.markdown:
1. Your app calls `openStoreSheet` with one of your short links. Strait records the tap (`sent_to = store_sheet` in [Analytics](https://straitlink.in/docs/analytics/)).
2. **Android:** the SDK opens Google Play's inline install, a half-sheet over your app. Google calls inline install a test feature; when Play can't show the sheet, it shows the full listing. If inline install isn't available, the SDK opens the Play app, then the Play web page. Every one of these carries `referrer=strait_link=<link>&strait_click=<tap>`, the same Play Install Referrer the redirect uses, so app B's first open matches exactly.
3. **iPhone (beta):** the SDK saves this device's match details for the tap, then shows `SKStoreProductViewController` (the full product page as a sheet) or `SKOverlay` (a small card). The link's campaign goes to the App Store as the campaign token. App B's first open finds the link through [iPhone install matching](https://straitlink.in/docs/iphone-install-matching/). If your workspace uses the clipboard boost, you can also have the SDK copy the one-time handoff link for an exact match.

sections.page: Store sheet (beta) — install another app without leaving yours
sections.markdown:
In Dashboard → Settings, the workspace needs the installed app's Android package name and, for iPhone, its App Store ID. The SDK reads them from Strait. You can also pass them in the call.

**You should see:** both fields filled in for the app being installed.

sections.page: Store sheet (beta) — install another app without leaving yours
Store sheet (beta) — install another app without leaving yours
sections.markdown:
```swift title="InstallButton.swift"
strait.openStoreSheet(
    url: "https://hilltop.strait.link/promo",
    options: StoreSheetOptions(style: .productPage), // or .overlay
    presenter: SystemStoreSheetPresenter(from: viewController)
) { result in
    print(result.method) // "product_page", "overlay" or "none"
}
```

`copyHandoffLink: true` copies the clipboard boost's one-time link as well. It's off by default, because it replaces whatever the user had copied.

**You should see:** the App Store product page as a sheet over your app.

sections.page: Store sheet (beta) — install another app without leaving yours
sections.markdown:
Both SDKs have `openStoreSheet` with the same options. Opening the store inside the app needs a small native module, because JavaScript and Dart can't start an Android Intent or show StoreKit:

- **React Native:** register a native module named `StraitStoreSheet` with `openIntent(intent)` (Android) and `presentProduct(product, style)` (iPhone). Without it, the SDK opens the Play app or the App Store app instead. The deep link is still kept, but the user leaves your app.
- **Flutter:** pass a `StoreSheetOpener`. The SDK README has a MethodChannel version.

**You should see:** `result.method` is `inline_install`, `product_page` or `overlay` with the native module, and `market` or `app_store` without it.

sections.page: Store sheet (beta) — install another app without leaving yours
sections.markdown:
Uninstall app B. In app A, tap your Install button, install app B from the sheet, then open it.

**You should see:** app B opens on the link's screen. In Dashboard → Analytics, the tap shows with `sent_to = store_sheet`, followed by the install.

sections.page: Store sheet (beta) — install another app without leaving yours
sections.markdown:
- It works only inside your own app. It can't open a store sheet inside another company's app.
- Android inline install is a Google Play test feature. Play decides when the sheet shows.
- iPhone: the deep link after install depends on install matching (beta) or the clipboard boost. Apple's App Store sheet doesn't pass any data to the installed app.
- Offline, the SDK can still open the store when you pass the package name or App Store ID, but the deep link isn't kept.

sections.page: Store sheet (beta) — install another app without leaving yours
sections.markdown:
- **`result.reason` is `no_package` or `no_app_store_id`.** The workspace has no package name or App Store ID for the installed app. Add it in Dashboard → Settings, or pass `androidPackage` / `appStoreId`.
- **Android opens the full Play listing, not the half-sheet.** Inline install is up to Google Play. Check that `callerId` is your own package name.
- **App B opens on its home screen.** The tap was offline (`result.reason` is `offline`), or on iPhone install matching found no match. Try again online; on iPhone, see [install matching](https://straitlink.in/docs/iphone-install-matching/).

sections.page: Store sheet (beta) — install another app without leaving yours
sections.markdown:
- [iPhone install matching](https://straitlink.in/docs/iphone-install-matching/): how the iPhone side finds the link after install.
- [Analytics: how we count](https://straitlink.in/docs/analytics/): where store sheet taps show up.

```txt
https://hilltop.strait.link/summer   →   https://shop.example.com/product/42
        └ link domain ┘ └slug┘        └──────── destination ────────┘
```

- **Slug**: letters, digits, `-` and `_`, up to 64 characters. A few words are reserved (`v1`, `healthz`, `debug`…). If a slug is already taken you get `409`.
- **Destination** (`longUrl`): must be `https://`. Your app receives its path and query (`/product/42`), so use the same paths your app routes on.

:::note No website?
The destination can be any `https://` URL on a domain you control, or your default web URL (Dashboard → Settings) with the path you want, such as `https://yourapp.com/product/42`. Only the path and query reach your app. Desktop visitors go to the full URL, and so do people without the app if you chose "always your website", so make sure that page exists.
:::

| Who taps | What happens |
|---|---|
| Android, app installed, verified link | The phone opens your app directly. The SDK resolves the link and reports the open. |
| Android, from a browser page | Our server hands the link to your app with your custom scheme. If the app isn't installed, the phone goes to Google Play (link kept for after install) or your website, as set in Settings. |
| iPhone, app installed | iOS opens your app directly via Universal Links. |
| iPhone, app not installed | Safari shows a page with a **Get the app** button that opens the App Store. The tap saves a short-lived match so the first open lands on the right screen (beta). |
| In-app browsers (Instagram, TikTok, X…) | These often don't open apps from a link on their own, so we show a page made for them: on Android, an **Open in app** button; everywhere, steps to open the link in the real browser. |
| Desktop | Redirects to the link's desktop URL, or the destination. |
| Link-preview robots (WhatsApp, Slack, iMessage…) | Get a preview page with the link's title, description and image. They're never redirected and never counted as taps. |

Every tap reaches Cloudflare first. What happens next depends on what the tap needs:

- **Plain redirects** are decided at the Cloudflare location nearest the person, without a round trip to our servers. This covers desktop taps, Android browser taps (to your app, Google Play or your website) and iPhone taps that go directly to the website or the App Store. The decision is made by the same code our server runs, so the person lands in the same place either way.
- **Everything else is served by our server**: pages (the iPhone **Get the app** page, in-app browser pages, password and expired pages), link-preview robots, and links with A/B destinations. A link close to its expiry time also goes to our server, so expiry is exact.

Both paths record the tap the same way: the same Analytics row, the same billing rules and the same `link.clicked` webhook. For a tap decided at the edge, the webhook is sent when our server receives the tap's record, a moment after the redirect. If that record can't be delivered right away, it's kept and sent again later.

When you change or deactivate a link, or change your workspace settings, taps follow the new version within 30 seconds. Changes made through the API take effect right away on our server and at the Cloudflare location that carried the request; other locations, and changes made in the dashboard, can take up to 30 seconds.

Each link can also have:

- **Per-platform fallbacks**: `iosFallbackUrl`, `androidFallbackUrl`, `desktopUrl` (all https).
- **Social preview**: title, description and image for chat-app previews.
- **Campaign, tags, folders and UTM parameters** to organise links and analytics.
- **Expiry**: after it, the link stops opening its destination. You choose where taps go instead (see below).
- **Password**: people must enter it before being redirected. Previews still work.
- **A/B destinations**: split taps across several destinations. Analytics shows which variant each tap got.
- **QR code**: download one for any link from the dashboard. [Branded QR codes](https://straitlink.in/docs/qr-codes/) add your colours, your app icon and an API.
- **Scheduled go-live**: share a link before launch and choose where early taps go. [Guide](https://straitlink.in/docs/scheduled-go-live/).
- **Country rules**: send people in chosen countries to their own web page. [Guide](https://straitlink.in/docs/country-rules/).

After its expiry time a link no longer opens its destination. You decide where people go instead. Set the default for every link in **Settings → When a link expires**, and change it for one link in its edit panel (or with the API fields below). A link with no setting of its own follows the workspace default.

| Option | What people see |
|---|---|
| **Show an 'expired' page** (default) | A short "This link has expired" page with your app's name and a link to your website. HTTP 410. |
| **Send to the app store** | Google Play on Android, the App Store on iPhone, using your app configuration. On Android the install referrer carries the tap, the same as any store hand-off. Computers, and phones whose store isn't set up, go to your expired-link web page if you set one, otherwise they see the expired page. |
| **Send to a web page** | Everyone goes to the https page you choose. If it's missing, or fails our phishing and malware check, people see the expired page instead. |

The store and web page options answer with a plain redirect (HTTP 302). Whichever option you pick, a tap on an expired link is recorded with **Sent to: expired**, plus where it went, and is never billed or sent as a `link.clicked` webhook. The dashboard Playground and `GET /v1/simulate` show the same decision as a real tap.

With the API, `POST /v1/links` and `PATCH /v1/links/{slug}` accept:

- `expiresAt`: epoch milliseconds or an ISO 8601 date-time (`null` in a PATCH removes the expiry).
- `expiredAction`: `page`, `store` or `url` (`null` in a PATCH goes back to the workspace default).
- `expiredUrl`: an https page. Required with `url`. With `store`, it's where computers go.

```bash
curl -X PATCH https://strait.link/v1/links/summer \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $STRAIT_SECRET_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"expiredAction":"url","expiredUrl":"https://yourco.com/offers"}'
```
Deactivating a link (dashboard, or `DELETE /v1/links/{slug}`) stops it resolving. Visitors see a not-found page that links to your website if one is set in Settings.
Links used for phishing, malware or spam are disabled under the [Acceptable Use Policy](https://straitlink.in/legal/acceptable-use/). A disabled link shows a warning page instead of redirecting.

Android App Links and iPhone Universal Links are verified **per domain**. The phone downloads a small file from the link's domain that says which app may open its links:

- `https://hilltop.strait.link/.well-known/assetlinks.json` (Android)
- `https://hilltop.strait.link/.well-known/apple-app-site-association` (iPhone)

If every customer shared one domain, that file could only name one app, and everyone else's links would open the browser. So each workspace gets its own subdomain, and we serve your app's files from it, built from the details in **Dashboard → Settings**.

A slug is unique within your workspace, not across Strait. Two workspaces can both have `/summer`: `https://hilltop.strait.link/summer` and `https://lemonlane.strait.link/summer` are different links that open different apps.

That's why you should **always share your handle URL**, never the bare `https://strait.link/summer`. The bare `strait.link` root only answers a slug that no other workspace uses, so links shared before workspaces had their own domains keep working. Once a second workspace creates the same slug, the bare address finds nothing. The API returns the right address for every link as `shortUrl`, and the dashboard copies it for you.

Your handle comes from your workspace name when you sign up (for example "Hilltop Shoes" becomes `hilltop-shoes`). Handles are 3 to 30 characters: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. Some words, like `www`, `api` and `status`, are reserved for our own use.

:::warn Choose your handle before your first link
The workspace owner can rename the handle in **Dashboard → Get started** (or **Settings**) until the workspace creates its first link. After that it's fixed, because links you've shared and the App Links / Universal Links setup in your app depend on it.
:::

Use your link domain in three places:

1. **The SDK `endpoint`**: `https://hilltop.strait.link`
2. **Android**: the `android:host` of your App Links intent filter
3. **iPhone**: the Associated Domains entry `applinks:hilltop.strait.link`

Custom domains are coming soon, and founding apps get them first. Today every workspace gets `<handle>.strait.link`, with HTTPS, on every plan. Serving links on your own domain (such as `links.yourcompany.com`) needs automatic certificates and domain verification, which we haven't built yet. We'll update this page when it's ready.

:::note
After changing your app's signing keys or team ID, phones and Google's verifier re-read the files on their own schedule. We serve them with a short cache (10 minutes), but Android can take longer to re-verify an installed app. Reinstalling the app forces a fresh check.
:::

A QR code is the link drawn as squares. Strait draws every code from one workspace style, so a code you download from the dashboard and one your server makes through the API look the same. Scans count as the **qr** channel in Analytics unless you turn that off.

Open **Dashboard → Settings → QR codes** and choose:

- **Code colour**: the squares. Empty means black.
- **Background**: behind the squares. Empty means white.
- **Put my app icon in the middle**: uses the app icon from **How your link pages look**. The code then uses the highest error correction level (H), so it still scans with the middle covered.

The colours must pass one rule: **the code must be darker than its background, with a contrast of at least 3:1**. Phone cameras look for dark squares on a light background, so light-on-dark codes and pale colour pairs are refused, in the dashboard and in the API. The form shows the contrast as you type. Then press **Save QR style**. Owners, admins and members can change it; viewers can only look.

**You should see:** the preview in your colours, a line under the colour fields like "Contrast 21.0:1: phone cameras will read it", and "Saved ✓" after you save.

sections.section: 2. Download a code from the dashboard
sections.markdown:
Go to **Dashboard → Links** and press **QR** on any link. The dialog shows the code in your style and the exact URL it opens. Keep **Count scans as the qr channel in Analytics** ticked to add `utm_source=qr` to the code, then pick a download:

| Button | You get |
|---|---|
| **Download PNG** | 1024 × 1024 px, for screens and documents |
| **PNG for print** | 2048 × 2048 px |
| **Download SVG** | Vector, sharp at any print size |

**You should see:** a file named after the link in your downloads (`summer-qr.png`, `summer-qr-2048.png` or `summer-qr.svg`), and the code opening the link when you scan it with a phone.

Call [`GET /v1/links/{slug}/qr`](https://straitlink.in/docs/api/get-link-qr/) with a secret key. It answers with the image itself, in the workspace style unless you override it for this one code:

| Query parameter | Values | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `format` | `png` or `svg` | `png` |
| `size` | 128 to 2048 px | 1024 |
| `margin` | 0 to 16 modules of quiet zone | 2 |
| `color`, `background` | hex, like `1f2937` | the workspace style |
| `logo` | `true` or `false` | the workspace style |
| `track` | `true` adds `utm_source=qr` | `true` |

```bash
curl "https://strait.link/v1/links/summer/qr?format=svg&color=1f2937" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SECRET_KEY" \
  --fail -o summer-qr.svg
```

```js title="Node 18+"
import { writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises';

const res = await fetch('https://strait.link/v1/links/summer/qr?format=png&size=2048', {
  headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.SECRET_KEY}` },
});
if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}: ${await res.text()}`);
await writeFile('summer-qr.png', Buffer.from(await res.arrayBuffer()));
console.log(res.headers.get('x-strait-qr-url'), res.headers.get('x-strait-qr-logo'));
```

Two response headers tell you what you got: `X-Strait-Qr-Url` is the exact URL in the code, and `X-Strait-Qr-Logo` says whether the icon went in (`embedded`, `off`, `no_icon`, `unavailable` or `png_needs_png_icon`). Python, PHP, Java and Go versions are on the [endpoint page](https://straitlink.in/docs/api/get-link-qr/). Write the colours without `#`, or as `%23` (a raw `#` starts the URL's fragment).

**You should see:** `summer-qr.svg` on disk, and `X-Strait-Qr-Url: https://hilltop.strait.link/summer?utm_source=qr`.

Scan a downloaded code with a phone, then open **Dashboard → Analytics**.

**You should see:** the tap under the **qr** channel, with where it went (app, store or website), like any other tap.

- **`400` "the QR colours are too close to scan reliably (contrast 2.1:1, needs 3:1)"**. Darken the code colour or lighten the background until the contrast is 3:1 or more. Plain black on white is always fine.
- **`400` "the QR colour must be darker than its background"**. Light codes on dark backgrounds are refused because many phone cameras miss them. Swap the two colours.
- **`X-Strait-Qr-Logo: png_needs_png_icon`**. Your app icon is a JPEG or WebP, and PNG codes can only embed a PNG icon. Ask for `format=svg`, or upload a PNG icon in Settings.

- [Analytics: how we count](https://straitlink.in/docs/analytics/): what a tap is, and how the qr channel is decided.
- [Get a branded QR code (API reference)](https://straitlink.in/docs/api/get-link-qr/): every parameter, the rate limit and all six languages.

Print the poster, schedule the WhatsApp broadcast and send the email before the sale starts. Until the go-live time, the link isn't live yet, and you choose where taps go. From that moment it opens its destination like any other link.

In **Dashboard → Links**, open the link's edit panel and fill in **Goes live**. The time is in your own time zone, which the label shows. Leave it blank for a link that is live now.

**You should see:** a **Goes live …** chip in the link's edit panel, with the date, time and time zone.

sections.section: 2. Choose where taps go before then
sections.markdown:
Once a go-live time is set, the panel asks **Before it goes live, send people to**:

| Option | What people see |
|---|---|
| **Show a 'coming soon' page** (default) | A short page saying the link isn't live yet and when it opens, with your app's name and a link to your website. |
| **Send to the app store** | Google Play on Android, the App Store on iPhone, from your app configuration, so people can install ahead of launch. Computers, and phones whose store isn't set up, go to the web page you give here, else the coming-soon page. |
| **Send to a web page** | Everyone goes to the https page you choose until the link goes live. |

Save the link.

**You should see:** your choice saved on the link. In the dashboard Playground, each device shows **Not live yet: gets the link's before-launch destination**.

sections.section: 3. Or do it with the API
sections.markdown:
[`POST /v1/links`](https://straitlink.in/docs/api/create-link/), [`POST /v1/links/batch`](https://straitlink.in/docs/api/batch-create-links/) and [`PATCH /v1/links/{slug}`](https://straitlink.in/docs/api/update-link/) accept:

- `startsAt`: epoch milliseconds or an ISO 8601 date-time. It must be before `expiresAt` if the link has one. In a PATCH, `null` makes the link live now.
- `notLiveAction`: `page`, `store` or `url`. Leave it out for the coming-soon page.
- `notLiveUrl`: an https page. Required with `url`; with `store`, it's where computers go. It passes the same phishing and malware check as every destination.

```bash
curl -X POST https://strait.link/v1/links \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SECRET_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "slug": "diwali-sale",
    "longUrl": "https://shop.example.com/sale/diwali",
    "startsAt": "2026-10-20T00:00:00+05:30",
    "notLiveAction": "store"
  }'
```

**You should see:** `201` with the link, including `startsAt` as epoch milliseconds and `notLiveAction: "store"`.

Ask [`GET /v1/simulate`](https://straitlink.in/docs/api/simulate-tap/) what a tap would do. It records nothing:

```bash
curl "https://strait.link/v1/simulate?url=https://hilltop.strait.link/diwali-sale&ua=android" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SECRET_KEY"
```

**You should see:** `"decision": "not_live"` and `"notLiveTo": "store"` before the go-live time, and the link's normal decision after it.

Taps before the go-live time **are not counted**: they aren't recorded in Analytics, never count toward your plan's taps, and send no `link.clicked` webhook. Link previews still work, so a link shared ahead of launch unfurls in WhatsApp and other chat apps with its title and image. After the go-live time, every tap is recorded and billed as usual.

- **`400` "startsAt must be before expiresAt"**. The link would expire before it goes live. Move one of the two times.
- **`400` "notLiveAction \"url\" needs notLiveUrl (an https URL)"**. Send `notLiveUrl` with `url`, or pick `page`.
- **`400` "notLiveUrl needs notLiveAction \"url\" or \"store\""**. The coming-soon page has no web page; drop `notLiveUrl` or change the action.

- [Country rules](https://straitlink.in/docs/country-rules/): send people in some countries to a different web page.
- [Short links](https://straitlink.in/docs/short-links/#when-a-link-expires): the other end of a link's life, where taps go after it expires.

One link on a global campaign can send India to your Indian store page and Bangladesh to its own page, without separate links.

Country rules **only change web and fallback destinations**: where someone lands in a browser. That is the computer destination, the per-platform fallbacks, the link's destination when it opens as a web page, and your workspace fallback. Opening your app on the right screen, and sending people to Google Play or the App Store, are unchanged, so deep links and deferred deep links behave exactly as before.

In **Dashboard → Links**, open the link's edit panel, find **Country rules** and press **Add a country rule**. Fill in:

- **Countries**: 2-letter country codes separated by commas, like `IN, BD`.
- **Web page**: the https page for people in those countries.

A link can have up to 5 rules, each with up to 50 countries. The first rule that lists the visitor's country wins. Save the link.

**You should see:** the rule saved on the link, and "Rule 1" with your countries and page when you open the panel again.

sections.section: 2. Or do it with the API
sections.markdown:
[`POST /v1/links`](https://straitlink.in/docs/api/create-link/), [`POST /v1/links/batch`](https://straitlink.in/docs/api/batch-create-links/) and [`PATCH /v1/links/{slug}`](https://straitlink.in/docs/api/update-link/) accept `countryRules`, a list of `{ countries, url }`. A PATCH replaces all of a link's rules; `null` or `[]` removes them.

```bash
curl -X PATCH https://strait.link/v1/links/summer \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SECRET_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "countryRules": [
      { "countries": ["IN"], "url": "https://shop.example.com/in/summer" },
      { "countries": ["BD", "NP"], "url": "https://shop.example.com/south-asia/summer" }
    ]
  }'
```

Country codes are trimmed and upper-cased for you. Every rule's page passes the same phishing and malware check as the link's destination.

**You should see:** `200` with the link, its `countryRules` listing both rules.

sections.section: 3. Test it as a visitor from another country
sections.markdown:
In the dashboard **Playground**, type a code in **Visitor's country (optional)**. Or ask [`GET /v1/simulate`](https://straitlink.in/docs/api/simulate-tap/), which records nothing:

```bash
curl "https://strait.link/v1/simulate?url=https://hilltop.strait.link/summer&ua=desktop&country=IN" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SECRET_KEY"
```

**You should see:** `"countryRule": true` and `location` set to your India page for `IN`, and the usual destination for a country without a rule. On a phone with your app installed, the decision is still to open the app.

The country is the one Cloudflare gives the request, from the visitor's network address. It is used to make this one decision and is never stored with the tap. When the country can't be told, no rule applies and the usual destination is used.

- **`400` "countryRules[0].countries: \"IND\" is not a 2-letter country code"**. Use ISO 3166-1 two-letter codes: `IN`, not `IND` or `India`.
- **`400` "countryRules allows at most 5 rules"**. Combine countries that share a page into one rule.
- **A rule doesn't change where the app opens.** That is by design: rules only replace web and fallback destinations. To send a country to a different screen in the app, use a separate link.

- [Scheduled go-live](https://straitlink.in/docs/scheduled-go-live/): share a link before launch and choose where early taps go.
- [Simulate a tap (API reference)](https://straitlink.in/docs/api/simulate-tap/): every decision the playground can show.

When someone without your app taps a link on Android, we send them to Google Play with the link attached to the install:

```txt
https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.yourco.app&referrer=strait_link%3D<link id>%26strait_click%3D<tap id>
```

Google Play keeps that referrer through the install. On first open, the SDK reads it, asks our server for the link (`/v1/referrer`), and routes your app there. It's **deterministic**: no guessing, and the install is joined to the exact tap.

To test it you need a build installed **from Google Play**. An internal testing track works. Sideloaded builds have no referrer.

If there's no referrer link (the app was found in a store search, for example), the SDK still checks in once so the install is counted in your match rate. Don't expect a match in that case on Android.

iOS doesn't pass anything through the App Store. You choose the method in **Dashboard → Settings → iPhone installs**: device matching (below), paste handoff (an exact one-time link the person allows to paste; reading it shows an "Allow Paste" prompt), both, or neither. Device matching starts off for new workspaces. Your app reads the choice from our server on its first open, so changing it needs no app release. Device matching works like this:

1. Someone without your app taps the link in Safari and sees a page with a **Get the app** button.
2. Tapping it records a coarse device signature together with the link, then opens the App Store.
3. On first launch, the SDK sends the same coarse fields to `/v1/match`. If a signature from the last **1 hour** matches, your app gets the link.

The signature is made from:

| Input | From |
|---|---|
| Screen width and pixel ratio | The browser, then the app |
| Language and time zone | The browser, then the app |
| iOS major version | The browser's user agent, then the app's |
| Network: prefix, operator (ASN) and a keyed hash of the full IP | Seen by our server; never sent by the app |

Each saved signature can be matched **once** and expires after one hour. It's never used to identify anyone across apps or sites.

What we use, how long we keep it, why there's no ATT prompt, the four combinations of the two switches, paste handoff (an exact match the person allows) and a ready-made App Store privacy label are all in [How iPhone install matching works](https://straitlink.in/docs/iphone-install-matching/).

:::warn Probabilistic, and in beta
Two people on the same network with the same phone model, language and time zone who tap different links within the hour are **not matched at all**: when taps look alike, we refuse rather than guess, so neither install is sent to the wrong screen. Each match in Analytics shows its method, so you can see how installs were matched. iPhone matching hasn't been proven on a real device yet.
:::

Either way, a matched install comes back to the app with its tap id, so purchases made afterwards are credited to that tap (see [Purchases](https://straitlink.in/docs/analytics/#purchases)).

Every install in Analytics shows how it was matched:

| Method | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `install_referrer` | Exact, from the Google Play referrer |
| `exact_ext` | iPhone signature matched on every input |
| `exact_core` | iPhone signature matched on the core inputs |
| `scored` | iPhone signals scored against recent taps; used only in workspaces where Strait has turned scored matching on |
| `clipboard` | iPhone clipboard boost: the one-time handoff link from the tap page (exact) |
| `none` | No match: organic install, or the match window passed |

The deferred check runs once per install. It's skipped (and marked done) when the first launch was itself opened by a link, so a direct open is never followed by a stale deferred jump. If the phone is offline on first launch, the check runs again next launch.

From the app details in **Dashboard → Settings**, your link domain serves:

| File | Built from | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| `/.well-known/assetlinks.json` | Package name + every SHA-256 fingerprint you list | Android, to verify App Links |
| `/.well-known/apple-app-site-association` | Apple Team ID + bundle ID | iPhone, to verify Universal Links |

Each file returns `404` until the matching fields are filled in. Check yours:

```bash
curl https://hilltop.strait.link/.well-known/assetlinks.json
curl https://hilltop.strait.link/.well-known/apple-app-site-association
```

Or paste your link domain into the [App Links checker](https://straitlink.in/tools/app-links-checker/), which checks both files and explains any problem.

1. Add an intent filter with `android:autoVerify="true"` for `https://hilltop.strait.link` ([example](https://straitlink.in/docs/production-checklist/#2-verify-app-links-on-android)).
2. List **every** certificate fingerprint your app is signed with in Settings: debug, upload, and the Play App Signing key from Play Console. A Play-installed app is signed by Google's key, not yours. Fingerprints are checked when you save: each one is stored as 32 uppercase hex pairs joined by colons (`FA:C6:17:…`), duplicates are dropped, and anything that isn't a SHA-256 fingerprint is refused. The package name must look like a Java package (`com.yourco.app`), and the website fallback must be `https://`.
3. Install the app. Android checks the file at install time.

Check verification on a connected phone:

```bash
adb shell pm get-app-links com.yourco.app
# Look for:  hilltop.strait.link: verified
```

If it says `1024` or `none`, Android couldn't verify. See [Troubleshooting](https://straitlink.in/docs/troubleshooting/#the-link-opens-the-browser-instead-of-the-app).

1. Add the **Associated Domains** capability with `applinks:hilltop.strait.link`.
2. Save your Apple Team ID and bundle ID in Settings.
3. Install the app. iOS fetches the file through Apple's CDN, which can lag behind changes.

When a tap can't open your app right away, the person sees one of our pages: the iPhone "Get the app" page, the page inside an in-app browser (Instagram, Facebook, WhatsApp…) with **Open in app**, the password page, and the "not found" and "This link has expired" pages. They lead with your app, not with Strait. Set these optional fields in **Dashboard → Settings → How your link pages look**:

| Field | Rules | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| App name | 1 to 60 characters, no line breaks | "Opens Hilltop Shoes…", "Go to Hilltop Shoes's website" |
| Icon URL | `https://` only (people's phones load it). Use a square image | The icon at the top of each page |
| Brand colour | A hex colour such as `#7c3aed` (`#abc` is fine too) | The main button. We pick black or white text on it so it stays readable (contrast at least 4.5:1) |

Invalid values are refused when you save, with a message saying why. Leave them empty and the pages use neutral defaults. Every page works in light and dark mode. The page we show for a link we've disabled for safety stays unbranded on purpose.

When a tap reaches our server in a browser (for example from a web page, or on Android when the link isn't verified), we hand the link to your app using your custom scheme:

```txt
yourapp://shop.example.com/product/42?strait_click=<tap id>
```

The SDK turns that into the destination `https://shop.example.com/product/42`, removes the tap id before your app sees it, and uses the id to join the app open to the exact tap in Analytics.

iOS passes nothing through the App Store. So when your app opens for the first time, it has to ask us "which link was this?" with nothing in hand but what the phone looks like and the network it's on.

We use that only to **open the right screen in the same app**: the screen behind the link the person just tapped. It routes one tap. We don't build a profile, follow anyone across apps or websites, or use it for advertising, and the signals are gone within about 2 days.

Strait has two ways to do this on iPhone. **You choose** which to use, with two switches in **Dashboard → Settings → iPhone installs**:

| Method | What it does | What the person sees |
|---|---|---|
| **Device matching** | The link page notes a few device and network details for up to an hour, and the app's first open is matched to them ([what we use](#what-we-use)). | Nothing: no prompt, no clipboard |
| **Paste handoff** (also called the [clipboard boost](#the-clipboard-boost-paste-handoff)) | **Get the app** copies a one-time link; the app reads it on its first open. Exact, single use, 24 hours. | iOS's "Allow Paste" prompt, or your app's Paste button |

Every combination works, and the dashboard shows a sentence for the one you picked:

| Device matching | Paste handoff | What happens on the app's first open |
|---|---|---|
| Off | Off | No deferred link on iPhone. People land on the app's home screen. Installs are still counted. |
| On | Off | Device matching only. If nothing matches, the app opens on its home screen. The clipboard is never read. |
| Off | On | Paste handoff only. No device details are kept. If the person doesn't allow the paste, the app opens on its home screen. |
| On | On | Device matching runs first. Only if it finds nothing does the app read the clipboard, so a device match never shows the paste prompt. |

**Defaults.** New workspaces start with both switches **off**, so nothing is matched until you choose. Workspaces created before 10 October 2026 keep the values they had.

**No app release needed.** The choice isn't built into your app. On its first open, the SDK asks our server `/v1/match`, and the answer carries your workspace's current choice. The SDK reads the clipboard only when that answer says paste handoff is on and device matching found nothing (or is off), and it doesn't keep the setting for later. So a change in the dashboard applies to versions already in the App Store, from the next first open (within about a minute).

When someone without your app taps **Get the app** on the link page in Safari, we save these signals with that tap. When your app opens for the first time, the SDK sends the same fields and our server compares them.

| Signal | Where it comes from | How we keep it |
|---|---|---|
| IP address | Seen by our server on the tap and on the first launch | Only as a **keyed hash** (HMAC-SHA256 with a server-side secret). The IP itself is never stored. |
| IPv6 /64 network | Seen by our server | Only as a keyed hash, like the IP |
| Network prefix (IPv4 /24 or IPv6 /48) and network operator number (ASN) | Seen by our server | As is |
| Screen size and pixel ratio | The browser, then the app | As is |
| Language and time zone | The browser, then the app | As is |
| iOS version (major) | The browser's user agent, then the app's | As is |

This is device data, and comparing it is a kind of device matching. We say so plainly so you can describe it accurately to your users and to Apple.

sections.section: How long we keep it, and what it's used for
sections.markdown:
- A tap's signals can be matched for **1 hour**. Our nightly cleanup erases them once that hour is a day old, so they're gone **within about 2 days of the tap** (at most 49 hours).
- They're used **only** to open the right screen in the same app that owns the link.
- One tap gives **at most one** match.
- When two taps look alike (for example two identical iPhones on one Wi-Fi network tapping different links), we **refuse** to match either of them rather than guess. The app then opens normally on its home screen.

- No advertising, and no measuring of advertising.
- No sharing or selling of this data, and no data brokers.
- No linking across apps: a match only ever happens inside the workspace that owns the link.
- No advertising identifier (IDFA), and no reading of anything else on the phone.

sections.section: Why there's no App Tracking Transparency prompt
sections.markdown:
Apple defines tracking as linking data collected in your app with other companies' data for targeted advertising or advertising measurement, or sharing it with data brokers ([Apple: User privacy and data use](https://developer.apple.com/app-store/user-privacy-and-data-use/)). Install matching does none of that: the data stays with your workspace and is used only to open your own app's screen. So it isn't tracking under that definition, and the SDK doesn't ask for ATT.

To be honest about the other side: Apple's page on required-reason APIs also says that fingerprinting is not allowed, whether or not a user gives permission to track. ATT doesn't change that. Device matching sits close to that line, and Apple decides what counts, so there is a risk that App Review flags it. That's why the choice is yours: device matching is off for new workspaces, you can [turn it on or off](#the-off-switch) at any time, and [paste handoff](#the-clipboard-boost-paste-handoff) on its own gives an exact match only after the person pastes, with no device details kept. The dashboard shows this note next to the Device matching switch. Each customer decides what's right for their app.

**Dashboard → Settings → iPhone installs → Device matching.** It's off for new workspaces; workspaces created before 10 October 2026 keep the value they had. Each switch saves as soon as you flip it.

When you turn it off:

- The link page stops saving these signals, and our server stores none.
- Signals already saved for your workspace are erased.
- A first launch on iPhone gets no match, so the app opens on its home screen (unless paste handoff finds the link).

Android isn't affected: it uses the Google Play Install Referrer, which carries the exact link through the install (see [Deferred deep linking](https://straitlink.in/docs/deferred-deep-linking/)).

Paste handoff, which we also call the clipboard boost, gives an **exact** match instead of a signal match, but only when the person pastes. It's off by default. Turn it on in **Dashboard → Settings → iPhone installs → Paste handoff**; that one switch is all it takes. The SDK learns it from `/v1/match` on the app's first open, so there is nothing to change in your app. (React Native, Flutter and Unity apps pass a clipboard adapter once, so the SDK can read the clipboard when your workspace asks for it.)

The old SDK option `clipboardBoost: true` is **deprecated and ignored**: the dashboard switch decides. You can leave it in your code or remove it.

How it works:

1. On the link page, **Get the app** also copies a one-time link to the clipboard. The link holds a random token. We store only a hash of it, it works **once**, and it expires after **24 hours**.
2. On the app's first launch, the SDK asks `/v1/match` first. If device matching is on and finds the install, the SDK never touches the clipboard and no prompt appears. Only if there's no match and the answer says paste handoff is on does the SDK check whether the clipboard probably holds a web link. iOS answers that without showing anything. If the server can't be reached, the SDK leaves the clipboard alone and tries again on the next launch.
3. Only if it does, the SDK reads the clipboard. **This shows iOS's "Allow Paste" prompt.** If the person allows it and the text is one of your handoff links, the SDK sends just the token to our server and the app opens the exact screen.
4. Instead of the prompt, you can show Apple's **Paste** button (`UIPasteControl` or SwiftUI `PasteButton`; the iOS SDK includes `StraitPasteButton`). Tapping it is the person's consent, and iOS shows no prompt.

The SDK never reads the clipboard unless your workspace has paste handoff on, and it sends nothing but a Strait handoff token. Anything else on the clipboard stays on the phone. If there's no token, or it was already used or has expired, the app gets the device-matching result. With both on, device matching runs first on the first launch and the clipboard is read only when it finds nothing, so most people never see the paste prompt. Both attempts count as one install.

A ready-made answer for **App Store Connect → App Privacy**, for the data the Strait SDK handles. It matches the SDK's privacy manifest (`PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy`). Add whatever else your own app collects.

| Data type | Purpose | Used for tracking | Linked to the user |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Coarse Location** (derived from the IP address) | App Functionality | No | No |
| **Other Data** (screen size, language, time zone, iOS version) | App Functionality | No | No |
| **Product Interaction** (link opens) | App Functionality; also Analytics if you use Strait analytics | No | No |

- **Used for tracking: No.** Nothing is combined with other companies' data for advertising or shared with data brokers.
- **Linked to the user: No**, because Strait has no user accounts or identity: no names, emails, phone numbers or advertising IDs. If you join Strait data (for example the tap id on a purchase) to your own user accounts, answer "Linked to the user" accordingly.
- The clipboard boost sends only a one-time token that Strait created, not the person's clipboard contents.

Our full data list is in the [Privacy policy](https://straitlink.in/legal/privacy/).

```txt
Taps  →  Where we sent them  →  App opened  →  Installs  →  Purchases
```

Each step is joined to the step before it with a tap id, so you can follow one tap all the way to revenue.

**Taps** are each time someone tapped one of your links.

- Taps that go through our server in a browser are counted when they arrive.
- A verified link can open your app directly from WhatsApp, Gmail and so on without touching our server. Those are counted when your app reports the open through the SDK.
- If a browser loads the link and then hands it to your app (Edge does this), it's still one tap.
- Link-preview robots are never counted.

**Where we sent them** is decided per device: app or store, app or website, store, website, the iPhone "Get the app" page, or the in-app-browser page. On Android the phone then makes the final choice: your app if installed, otherwise the store or website.

- **Opened the app**: browser taps where your app then opened and reported that exact tap, plus verified-link opens.
- **Open rate**: taps that opened the app (directly or via the browser), divided by all taps.
- **New users**: the first launch after installing the app. **Existing users**: already had it installed.
- **App state** at open: *closed* (the link launched the app), *background* (it brought the app back), *foreground* (the app was already on screen).
- **Unresolved opens**: a link opened the app but couldn't be resolved (expired, deleted, wrong workspace), so the person didn't land on the right screen.

Opens are reported once each. If the phone is offline, the SDK saves the report and sends it later (up to 7 days), and duplicates are ignored.

- **Installs from links**: first launches of a new install that we tied to one of your links.
- **Joined to the exact tap**: of those, the ones matched to the precise tap (Play install referrer or browser hand-off), not just the link.
- **Unattributed installs**: first launches no link could be found for: store search, word of mouth, or a match that failed.
- **Match rate**: installs reconnected to a tap, divided by all attributable installs.
- **Time to install**: the median time between tap and install, for installs matched to their tap.
- **Probably reached the store / website**: store-bound browser taps where the app never opened and no install followed. We can't see the store page itself, so these are estimates and labelled as such.

Send events from your app (`trackEvent`) or server (`POST /v1/event`) with an optional value, currency and link id. They appear as the last step of the funnel, with revenue.

Events can also carry `clickId`, the tap they came from, so revenue lands on that tap's channel and A/B variant. The app SDKs fill it in for you from the most recent link open within 7 days. The tap id reaches the app four ways: in a browser hand-off, in the Google Play install referrer, and in our server's answer when it matches an open from a verified short link or an iPhone install. Each newer open replaces the remembered tap with its own. An explicit `clickId` overrides it. A `clickId` that isn't a tap of your workspace is dropped, and the event is still recorded.

**An install that is never opened.** Until your app launches, no linking product can see it. Only Google Play Console and App Store Connect report raw installs. Expect our install numbers to be lower than the stores' for that reason.

Taps keep the network prefix (first three parts of the IP address, never the full address), platform, device class and OS version. App opens store the host and path of the URL, never the query string. See the [Privacy Policy](https://straitlink.in/legal/privacy/).

| Key | Looks like | Where it goes | What it can do |
|---|---|---|---|
| Publishable key | `st_pub_live_…` | Your app and website | Resolve links, report opens, match installs, send events |
| Secret key | `st_live_…` | Your server only | Create, list, update and deactivate links, export, send events |

The publishable key is in **Dashboard → Get started**. Secret keys are in **Dashboard → Settings → Secret keys**. Never put a secret key in an app or a web page: anyone can read it from there. When your app needs a new link (a share button, a referral), it asks your server, and your server calls the API with the secret key. See [Create links in the app](https://straitlink.in/docs/sdks/react-native/create-links/).

**Publishable key.** Rotate it in **Dashboard → Get started**. You get a new key right away, and the old one keeps working for **7 days**, so apps already on people's phones keep working while you ship an update with the new key. During those 7 days, responses to the old key carry a `Strait-Key-Deprecated` header with the time it stops working (ISO 8601, for example `2026-01-08T12:00:00.000Z`). After that, the old key gets `401`. If you rotate again within the 7 days, the key from the earlier rotation stops at once: only one old key is honoured.

**Secret keys.** You can have several. Each one in **Dashboard → Settings → Secret keys** shows when it was last used ("never used" if it hasn't been), so you can spot a key nothing uses any more before you revoke it. We store only a hash, so a new key is shown once. Revoking a secret key stops it immediately. To replace one without downtime, create the new key, deploy it, check the old key's last-used date has stopped moving, then revoke the old one.
Revoke it in **Dashboard → Settings → Secret keys** and create a new one. Revoking takes effect on the next request. Then check **Links** for changes you didn't make.

The SDK isn't on the npm registry yet, so install it from GitHub (npm builds it during install). It installs as `@straitlink/node`, so imports stay the same once it's on npm.

```bash
npm install github:bazingga08/strait-sdk-node#v0.6.3
```

| Method | Endpoint |
|---|---|
| `createLink(input)` | [`POST /v1/links`](https://straitlink.in/docs/api/create-link/) |
| `listLinks()` | [`GET /v1/links`](https://straitlink.in/docs/api/list-links/) |
| `updateLink(slug, fields)` | [`PATCH /v1/links/:slug`](https://straitlink.in/docs/api/update-link/) |
| `deleteLink(slug)` | [`DELETE /v1/links/:slug`](https://straitlink.in/docs/api/deactivate-link/) |
| `sendEvent(input)` | [`POST /v1/event`](https://straitlink.in/docs/api/send-event/) |

Full request and response details are in the [REST API reference](https://straitlink.in/docs/api/).

```txt
https://strait.link
```

Every endpoint has its own page, with the request in curl, Node, Python, PHP, Java and Go next to the response: see [Endpoints](#endpoints) below. The PHP, Java and Go examples use only the standard library (ext-curl, `java.net.http`, `net/http`).

Server recipes: [create links in bulk](https://straitlink.in/docs/recipes/batch-create-links/), [verify webhook signatures](https://straitlink.in/docs/recipes/verify-webhook-signatures/) and [send links in WhatsApp templates](https://straitlink.in/docs/recipes/whatsapp-template-links/).

- **[Download the OpenAPI description](https://straitlink.in/docs/api/openapi.json)** (also served live at `https://strait.link/v1/openapi.json`) for Insomnia or a code generator.
- **[Download the Postman collection](https://straitlink.in/docs/api/postman-collection.json)**: in Postman, **Import**, pick the file, then set `secretKey` and `publishableKey` in the collection's variables.

| Key | Send it as | Use it for |
|---|---|---|
| Secret key `st_live_…` | `Authorization: Bearer st_live_…` header | Link endpoints, and events from your server |
| Publishable key `st_pub_live_…` | `"publishableKey"` in the JSON body | Endpoints your app or website calls |

The publishable key is in **Dashboard → Get started** and secret keys are in **Dashboard → Settings → Secret keys**. The examples on this page read the secret key from an environment variable:

```bash
export SECRET_KEY=st_live_…   # Dashboard → Settings → Secret keys
```

 The publishable key is safe to ship in apps; it can only resolve links, report opens, match installs and send events. Requests with a missing or wrong key get `401`.

After you rotate the publishable key, the old key keeps working for 7 days so apps already on people's phones don't break. Responses to the old key carry a `Strait-Key-Deprecated` header with the time it stops working (ISO 8601, for example `Strait-Key-Deprecated: 2026-01-08T12:00:00.000Z`); after that it gets `401`. See [Keys](https://straitlink.in/docs/keys/#rotating-keys).

Every error under `/v1` is JSON with an `error` message, never an HTML page:

```json
{ "error": "slug already exists in this workspace" }
```

| Status | When |
|---|---|
| `400` | Invalid input, including a body that isn't valid JSON (`{ "error": "malformed JSON body" }`) |
| `401` | Missing or wrong key |
| `402` | Plan limit reached when creating a link. Adds `reason` (`"links"`, or `"clicks"` for the monthly tap limit) and `upgradeUrl`; existing links keep working |
| `404` | Not found, including unknown `/v1` paths (`{ "error": "not found" }`) |
| `409` | The slug is already used by an active link in your workspace |
| `413` | Request body too large |
| `429` | Rate limited |
| `500` | Our fault: `{ "error": "internal error" }`, with no internal details |

Some errors add fields, for example a blocked destination returns `{ "error": "destination_blocked", "reason": "…" }`. The endpoints apps call are rate-limited per IP address; normal SDK traffic is far below the limit.

Slugs are unique within your workspace, not across Strait: another workspace can also have `/summer` on its own link domain. Every link the API returns includes `shortUrl`, the address to share: `https://<your-handle>.strait.link/<slug>`. Always share `shortUrl`. See [Link domains](https://straitlink.in/docs/link-domains/).

Fetch one link by its slug with `GET /v1/links/{slug}`.

Link edits (`PATCH /v1/links/{slug}`) and deactivations (`DELETE /v1/links/{slug}`) apply to taps within 30 seconds. They apply right away on our server and at the Cloudflare location that carried your request; plain redirects decided at other Cloudflare locations can follow the old version for up to 30 seconds. See [How a tap is handled](https://straitlink.in/docs/short-links/#how-a-tap-is-handled).

`GET /v1/links` without parameters returns every active link as a plain JSON array. Add `limit` (1 to 100, default 50) or `cursor` to page through them instead, newest first:

```bash
curl "https://strait.link/v1/links?limit=50" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SECRET_KEY"
# → { "links": [ … ], "nextCursor": "WyIyMDI2…" }

curl "https://strait.link/v1/links?limit=50&cursor=WyIyMDI2…" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SECRET_KEY"
# → { "links": [ … ], "nextCursor": null }   ← the last page
```

Pass each `nextCursor` back as `cursor` until it is `null`. Treat the cursor as opaque; an invalid one gets `400`.

sections.section: Try a link without tapping it
sections.markdown:
`GET /v1/simulate` tells you what a tap would do, without recording a tap, sending webhooks or counting toward your plan. Pass the full short link as `url` and either a raw user agent or one of these presets as `ua`: `android`, `iphone`, `ipad`, `desktop`, `instagram-ios`, `instagram-android`, `facebook-android`, `whatsapp-android`, `bot`.

```bash
curl "https://strait.link/v1/simulate?url=https%3A%2F%2Fhilltop.strait.link%2Fsummer&ua=instagram-android" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SECRET_KEY"
```

The answer has the `decision` (`redirect`, `interstitial`, `escape`, `preview`, `expired` or `blocked`), `sentTo` (the same values as Analytics, below), the `location` the visitor would be sent to (or the main button's target on a page), and a plain-English `reason`. Hand-off URLs in it carry a placeholder tap id, `00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000`. You can also authenticate with `publishableKey=` as a query parameter; the link must belong to the key's workspace. **Dashboard → Playground** runs the same check.

Each tap is recorded with where we sent it, `sent_to` (in the taps export and the `sentTo` webhook field):

| `sent_to` | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `app_or_store` | Android: your app if installed, otherwise the store |
| `app_or_website` | Android: your app if installed, otherwise your website |
| `store` | Directly to Google Play or the App Store |
| `website` | Directly to the destination or fallback website |
| `app_store_page` | The iPhone "Get the app" page |
| `in_app_browser_page` | The page shown inside an in-app browser (Instagram, Facebook, WhatsApp…) with "Open in app" |
| `expired` | The link had expired: the visitor saw "This link has expired". Recorded, never billed, no webhook |

Taps decided at Cloudflare's edge and taps served by our server are recorded with the same fields and labels.

A tap's **channel** is the first of these that has a value: the tap URL's `utm_source`, the link destination's `utm_source`, the in-app browser it was tapped in (`whatsapp`, `instagram`…), then the referring site. Taps with none of these are direct.

A link's **campaign** is the `campaign` you set. If you leave it out, it's filled in from the destination's `utm_campaign`, and follows it when you change the destination.

`POST /v1/links` also accepts these optional fields (all URLs must be https):

| Field | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `iosFallbackUrl`, `androidFallbackUrl`, `desktopUrl` | Where to send people on that platform when the app can't open |
| `title`, `description`, `imageUrl` | The preview shown in chat apps and social posts |
| `campaign` | Campaign name for analytics (also passed to the App Store as the campaign token). Defaults to the destination's `utm_campaign` |
| `tags` | Labels for filtering |
| `expiresAt` | When the link expires: epoch milliseconds or an ISO 8601 date-time |
| `expiredAction`, `expiredUrl` | Where taps go after expiry: `page`, `store` or `url` (with an https `expiredUrl`). Leave out to use the workspace setting. See [When a link expires](https://straitlink.in/docs/short-links/#when-a-link-expires) |

`PATCH /v1/links/{slug}` changes `longUrl`, `title`, `tags`, `expiresAt`, `expiredAction` and `expiredUrl`. Send only what changes; `null` clears `expiresAt` (never expires) and `expiredAction` (back to the workspace setting).

`POST /v1/links/batch` creates up to 500 links in one call, for imports and migrations. Send `{ "links": [ … ] }`, where each item takes the same fields as `POST /v1/links`. Every item is checked the same way (slug rules, https destinations, the unsafe-destination check, plan limits) and gets its own result, so one bad item never fails the batch:

```bash
curl https://strait.link/v1/links/batch \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SECRET_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "links": [ { "slug": "spring", "longUrl": "https://shop.example.com/spring" },
                  { "slug": "summer", "longUrl": "https://shop.example.com/summer", "campaign": "summer_2026" } ] }'
# → { "results": [ { "index": 0, "ok": true, "status": 201, "link": { … } }, … ],
#     "summary": { "total": 2, "created": 2, "failed": 0 } }
```

The response is `200` whenever the request itself is valid; read each item's `ok` and `status` (`201`, `400`, `402` or `409`). A slug that already exists, or repeats earlier in the same batch, is a `409` for that item only, so re-running an import is safe. Items past a plan limit get `402`. See [Migrate from Branch](https://straitlink.in/docs/migrate-from-branch/).

Export everything in your workspace at any time, on every plan. It gives you what you need to leave, or to keep your links running if Strait ever shuts down. Send your secret key; a publishable key gets `401`.

```txt
GET https://strait.link/v1/export?part=links|taps|events|webhooks|worker
Authorization: Bearer st_live_…
```

| `part` | What you get |
|---|---|
| `links` | NDJSON, one link per line: slug, destination, platform fallbacks and whether it is active |
| `taps` | CSV of every tap, joined to the app opens and installs that came from it. No date cap; add optional `from` and `to` (ISO dates) to narrow it |
| `events` | CSV of every conversion event (signups, purchases, revenue): `created_at, name, value, currency, platform, link_id, slug, click_id, channel, campaign, variant`. `channel`, `campaign` and `variant` come from the tap the event is attributed to, when it has a `click_id`. Oldest first, no date cap; optional `from` and `to` |
| `webhooks` | JSON of your webhook settings: `url`, `events`, `active` and `createdAt` for each one. Signing secrets are never exported; make new ones when you recreate a webhook |
| `worker` | A single-file Cloudflare Worker with the Android, iPhone and desktop fallbacks built in. Deploy it on your own account and route a link domain you own to it, and links on that domain keep redirecting. It can't serve `strait.link` links (that domain is ours), and custom domains are coming soon |

```bash
curl "https://strait.link/v1/export?part=events&from=2026-01-01" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SECRET_KEY" -o events.csv
```

Taps and events are streamed page by page, so an export of millions of rows starts right away and never times out on our side.

### Download from the dashboard

Owners and admins can download every part from **Dashboard → Settings → Download everything**: one button per file, no secret key needed. Members and viewers can't, because an export contains all of the workspace's data. The same section keeps the commands above under **Or from your server**.

Each button asks for a one-time download link, then your browser saves the file directly, however large:

```txt
POST https://strait.link/v1/export/token      {"part": "events"}
→ 201 {"token": "stx_…", "expiresAt": "…", "path": "/v1/export?part=events&token=stx_…"}
GET  https://strait.link/v1/export?part=events&token=stx_…
```

The token works once, for 60 seconds, for that part (and its `from` / `to`) only. Only a hash of it is stored. A used or expired token gets `401`.

The SDKs call the publishable-key endpoints for you; you only need those if you're writing your own client.

In **Dashboard → Settings → Webhooks**, add an `https://` URL and pick events. You'll see the **signing secret** once; store it on your server. Free includes 1 webhook, Starter 3 and Scale 10 ([pricing](https://straitlink.in/pricing/)).

The URL must be a public `https://` address. When you save it, we refuse:

- `http://` and other schemes, and URLs with a username or password in them
- `localhost`, and hosts ending in `.localhost`, `.local` or `.internal`
- IP addresses in private, loopback, link-local, carrier-grade NAT (100.64.0.0/10), multicast and reserved ranges, IPv4 and IPv6

We check again before every delivery, after looking up the hostname, because DNS can change after you save. A URL that now points at a private address isn't sent to and isn't retried.

Press **Send test event** next to a webhook in **Dashboard → Settings → Webhooks**. We send one `ping` event to it right away, signed like every other delivery, and show what your server answered: the status code, the first 500 characters of the response body and how long it took. It works on a paused webhook too. Test events aren't stored or retried.

From your server, call the same thing with your secret key:

```bash
curl -X POST https://strait.link/v1/webhooks/<webhook id>/test \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SECRET_KEY"
```

```json title="Response"
{
  "delivered": true,
  "status": 204,
  "error": null,
  "body": "",
  "durationMs": 182,
  "deliveryId": "0b9c3f0e-5a7d-4a51-9a2e-3f1c8d2b6e47",
  "event": "ping"
}
```

When the delivery fails, `delivered` is `false` and `error` says why: `HTTP 500` (your server's status), `timeout` (no answer within 5 seconds) or `unsafe_target` (the URL resolves to a private address). An unknown webhook id, or one from another workspace, gets `404`.

| Event | Sent when | `data` fields |
|---|---|---|
| `link.clicked` | Someone taps a link (browser taps, and verified-link opens your app reports) | `linkId`, `slug`, `platform`, `clickId`, `sentTo`, `deviceClass`, `variant`, `source` |
| `install.matched` | A first launch after install is matched to a link | `linkId`, `clickId`, `matchMethod`, `platform` |
| `app.opened` | A link opens your app | `linkId`, `clickId`, `kind`, `route`, `appState`, `isInstall`, `matched`, `platform` |
| `ping` | You send a test event | `webhookId`, `message` |
| `referral.converted` | Preview, not switched on yet: a referred install opens and matches its tap ([Referrals](https://straitlink.in/docs/referrals/)) | `referralCode`, `linkId`, `clickId`, `platform`, `matchMethod` |

Fields that don't apply to an event are left out. Taps on an expired link are recorded in Analytics but don't send `link.clicked`.

```http title="Request we send"
POST /your/webhook HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: application/json
X-Strait-Event: install.matched
X-Strait-Delivery: 7f3e2c1a-9b4d-4e8f-a6c5-2d1b0e9f8a73
X-Strait-Attempt: 1
X-Strait-Signature: t=1767225600,v1=6a1f0c3e9b…

{
  "id": "7f3e2c1a-9b4d-4e8f-a6c5-2d1b0e9f8a73",
  "event": "install.matched",
  "createdAt": "2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
  "data": {
    "linkId": "lnk_123",
    "clickId": "c_123",
    "matchMethod": "install_referrer",
    "platform": "android"
  }
}
```

- Each request times out after 5 seconds. Respond quickly with any `2xx` and do the work afterwards.
- Redirects aren't followed: a `3xx` counts as a failed attempt.
- **Retries:** anything other than a `2xx` (or no answer) is retried after 30 seconds, 2 minutes, 10 minutes, 1 hour and 6 hours, six attempts in total, then marked failed. Your server can be down for hours without losing events.
- Each event has a stable id: `X-Strait-Delivery` (the same as `id` in the body) stays the same on every retry, and `X-Strait-Attempt` counts up. Store the ids you've handled and ignore repeats: delivery is **at least once**.
- Every attempt is signed again with a fresh timestamp, so a retry six hours later still passes the 5-minute check.
- Addresses that resolve to private networks are never sent to or retried.

Open **Deliveries** under a webhook in **Dashboard → Settings → Webhooks** to see its last 20 deliveries: the event, when it was created, its status (**Delivered**, **Retrying** or **Failed** after all six attempts), how many attempts it took and your server's last answer. A failed delivery, or one waiting for its next retry, has a **Redeliver** button: fix your endpoint (or change the webhook URL), press it, and we send the same event again right away. Owners, admins and members can redeliver; viewers can only look.

The same from your server, with a secret key:

```txt
GET https://strait.link/v1/webhooks/{id}/deliveries?limit=20&cursor=…
Authorization: Bearer st_live_…
```

```json
{
  "deliveries": [
    {
      "id": "7f3e2c1a-9b4d-4e8f-a6c5-2d1b0e9f8a73",
      "webhookId": "5d0c…",
      "event": "link.clicked",
      "status": "failed",
      "attempts": 6,
      "lastStatus": 500,
      "lastError": "HTTP 500",
      "nextAttemptAt": null,
      "createdAt": "2026-10-04T09:12:03.512Z",
      "deliveredAt": null
    }
  ],
  "nextCursor": null
}
```

Newest first, `limit` 1 to 100 (default 20); pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` for the next page. Payloads aren't returned. `nextAttemptAt` is set while a delivery is waiting for a retry.

```txt
POST https://strait.link/v1/webhook-deliveries/{id}/redeliver
Authorization: Bearer st_live_…
```

This queues the delivery again with its attempt count reset, sends it at once to the webhook's **current** URL with the same `X-Strait-Delivery` id, and answers with the delivery after that attempt (same shape as above). If it fails again it gets the full retry schedule. You get `409` when it was already delivered, or while it's being sent (in its first 2 minutes, or claimed by a delivery worker right now): try again shortly. A delivery from another workspace is `404`.

Delivery history is kept for 30 days, then deleted by a nightly job.

:::warn Preview, not switched on yet
Referrals are built and tested, but they are not switched on in production yet, and the details below may change before they are. Until then, use the [invite-link flow that works today](https://straitlink.in/solutions/referrals/): put the code in the link's destination and read it in `onLink`. Want to try the preview? [Talk to us](https://straitlink.in/contact/).
:::

1. **A code on the tap.** Each tap can carry a referral code: either the link's own code, or a code added to the link's address for that one tap.
2. **The code survives the install.** When the person installs your app and opens it, the deferred answer your app gets on first open includes `referralCode`. On Android this comes through the Google Play install, so it's exact. On iPhone it comes through install matching, which is in [beta](https://straitlink.in/docs/iphone-install-matching/).
3. **Your server hears about it.** A `referral.converted` webhook fires once for each referred install that opens and matches. It carries the code, the link and the tap it came from.
4. **You see it per code.** The dashboard's Referrals page (preview) shows, for each code, the taps that carried it and the referred installs.

Strait doesn't grant rewards, hold credits or pay anyone out. That stays with your server, which decides from the webhook what each person gets.

sections.section: Two ways to attach a code
sections.markdown:
**One link per referrer.** Your server creates a link for each user and sets `referralCode`:

```bash
curl https://strait.link/v1/links \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SECRET_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "slug": "invite-asha", "longUrl": "https://shop.example.com/invite", "referralCode": "ASHA42" }'
```

The answer echoes `"referralCode": "ASHA42"`. If it doesn't, the code wasn't saved: referrals aren't switched on yet, or the save failed.

**One shared link, a code per tap.** Add `strait_ref` to any of your links:

```text
https://hilltop.strait.link/invite?strait_ref=ASHA42
```

A tap's own `strait_ref` wins over the link's code. A tap with two different `strait_ref` values counts as having no code.

A code is 1 to 64 letters, digits, `-` or `_`. Use your own user id or an invite code. Don't use an email address or a phone number: codes appear in links that people share.

The first-open answer (from `/v1/referrer` on Android, `/v1/match` or `/v1/handoff/claim` on iPhone) gains one field when the matched tap carried a code:

```json
{
  "matched": true,
  "longUrl": "https://shop.example.com/invite",
  "linkId": "lnk_…",
  "clickId": "6f1c…",
  "matchMethod": "install_referrer",
  "referralCode": "ASHA42"
}
```

If the tap had no code, or the install didn't match a tap, the answer has no `referralCode`, exactly as today. The SDK update that ships with the switch-on passes it to your app as `referralCode` on the deferred link event (React Native, Flutter, Android, iOS) or on the `resolveDeferredLink` result (web). Grant rewards from your server, using the webhook below, not in the app.

Subscribe to `referral.converted` in Dashboard → Settings → Webhooks (it shows there with a Preview badge once referrals are switched on). Deliveries are signed like every other [webhook](https://straitlink.in/docs/webhooks/):

```json
{
  "id": "…",
  "event": "referral.converted",
  "createdAt": "2026-10-05T10:40:00.000Z",
  "data": {
    "referralCode": "ASHA42",
    "linkId": "lnk_…",
    "clickId": "6f1c…",
    "platform": "android",
    "matchMethod": "install_referrer"
  }
}
```

It fires **once per tap**. If the app retries its first-open call, or the same tap leads to a reinstall, no second event is sent. A friend who already had your app opens it directly, so there is no install and no `referral.converted` event. Tell new users from existing ones with the `app.opened` event's `isInstall` field.

`GET /v1/referrals?from=2026-10-01&to=2026-10-31` (secret key) returns each code's taps and referred installs in that range, plus totals, with `"preview": true`. The dashboard's Referrals page shows the same numbers. A tap counts at the time of the tap, and a referred install at the time of the first open.

- No rewards, credits, payouts, fraud scoring or per-referrer caps. These belong in your server.
- The code is set when a link is created. It doesn't appear on the link list or edit endpoints yet, and the batch endpoint doesn't take it.
- Direct opens (the app was already installed) don't carry the code.
- The endpoint and fields above are in the [REST API reference](https://straitlink.in/docs/api/), marked preview. They may change before referrals are switched on.

- [Referral and invite links](https://straitlink.in/solutions/referrals/): the flow that works today

sections.page: Create links in bulk from your backend (batch API)
sections.markdown: Use the batch endpoint when you make links from data: one per product in a catalogue, per store, per referral partner, or a whole import from another provider. One call to [`POST /v1/links/batch`](https://straitlink.in/docs/api/batch-create-links/) takes up to 500 links, checks each one exactly like [`POST /v1/links`](https://straitlink.in/docs/api/create-link/), and answers with one result per item. For a single link at checkout or signup, call `POST /v1/links` instead.

sections.page: Create links in bulk from your backend (batch API)
sections.section: 1. Build the list with your own slugs
sections.markdown:
Give every link a slug you can work out again from your own data, like `p-42` for product 42 or `store-blr-07`. Slugs are 1 to 64 letters, digits, `_` or `-`, and unique in your workspace. Because you choose them, running the same job twice can't create a second copy: the second run gets `409` for slugs that already exist.

Each item takes the same fields as a single link. Put UTM tags on the destination so Analytics knows the channel and campaign without extra work:

```json title="One item"
{
  "slug": "p-42",
  "longUrl": "https://shop.example.com/product/42?utm_source=catalogue&utm_campaign=diwali-2026",
  "title": "Brass diya set",
  "tags": ["catalogue"]
}
```

**You should see:** a list where no slug appears twice. A repeat inside one call is a `409` for the later item ("slug repeats item 3 of this batch").

sections.section: 3. Store the short links next to your data
sections.markdown:
Each created item carries `shortUrl` (like `https://hilltop.strait.link/p-42`) and `id`. Save `shortUrl` on your product, store or partner row, so your emails, WhatsApp messages and invoices read it from your own database instead of calling the API again.

**You should see:** your table filled with `shortUrl` values, and the same links in **Dashboard → Links** when you filter by the tag you set.

sections.page: Create links in bulk from your backend (batch API)
sections.markdown:
Read `status` and `error` for each item in `failed`:

| `status` | What it means | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `400` | A field is wrong (slug rules, a non-https URL), or `error` is `destination_blocked` | Fix the item. `reason` says why a destination was blocked. |
| `402` | Your plan's link limit is reached | Upgrade, or deactivate links you no longer use |
| `409` | The slug already exists (counted as `existing` above) | Nothing, if it's your earlier run. To point it somewhere new, [update the link](https://straitlink.in/docs/api/update-link/). |

**You should see:** an empty `failed` list after you fix those items and run the job again.

sections.page: Create links in bulk from your backend (batch API)
sections.markdown:
- **The whole call gets `400`.** `links` is missing, empty or longer than 500. Split the list into calls of 500, as in step 2.
- **The whole call gets `401`.** The key is missing, or it's a publishable key (`st_pub_live_…`). Batch needs a secret key (`st_live_…`), from your server only.
- **Items come back `409` on the very first run.** The slugs clash with links someone made in the dashboard, or repeat inside your list. Add a prefix per job, like `diwali-p-42`.
